The neuron doctrine states that the neuron (nerve cell) is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system, physically separated from adjacent neurons by synapses. This doctrine emerged from a scientific debate in the late 19th century.  

Camillo Golgi, using his silver stain technique, proposed the reticular theory, which described the nervous system as a continuous network (reticulum) of interconnected cells. Thus, the neuron doctrine, foundational to modern neuroscience, was established through Cajal's microscopic work and Waldeyer's synthesis, resolving the debate in favor of discrete neuronal units.
